submission.natural_language_explanation: L2H0 is a phrase-frame routing head: at each token it attends back (typically weight 0.4-0.95) to the earlier token that opens the current phrase, most strongly a superlative marker (the/-est/best/worst/most), and fires while that phrase completes, peaking on the head noun or its closing qualifier (in/of/on/ever). It peaks strongest on superlative noun phrases and moderately on code declaration lines and performative frames such as 'I apologize for'; plain prose with no such opener reads weak, mostly below the active line.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Our bus rolled out of the depot while dawn painted the rooftops gold. The driver waved toward the hills and called out each stop by name. Passengers traded bread and olives across the aisle as children stared through dusty panes. We crossed a wide river where herons stood motionless along the banks. A vendor boarded with trays of apricots and almonds, shouting prices that made everyone laugh. The road climbed past terraced orchards and whitewashed cottages with blue shutters. Goats scattered near a stone bridge while a shepherd raised his arm in greeting. We paused at a roadside café where the owner poured coffee from a copper pot. Maps were unfolded, routes argued over, and coins counted twice. The train depot came after noon, its platform crowded with baskets and bicycles. Our carriage smelled of cedar and rain. Hills gave way to plains dotted with windmills and haystacks. A conductor punched tickets and pointed out an old castle on a ridge. Ducks paddled beside the track where canals branched toward distant farms. We shared lunch with a teacher who marked our route in pencil. The rails hummed under a sky full of slow clouds. At dusk the city glowed ahead, its harbor lined with lamps. Boats rocked gently while gulls circled the masts. A guide met us carrying a lantern and led us uphill. Porters hauled luggage up worn stairways past shuttered shops. Drums echoed from a square where dancers spun in circles. The night air smelled of jasmine and charcoal smoke. We slept in a hostel courtyard under a plain canvas awning. Roosters woke us before sunrise and bread arrived warm. A boat carried us across the bay toward green cliffs. Dolphins surfaced near the bow as cameras clicked. The captain pointed to caves carved by the surf. We hiked a narrow trail above the water with ropes along the rim. Picnic hampers were opened on flat rocks overlooking the surf. The path wound down to a cove with black sand. Children chased crabs while elders napped in the shade. A second trail climbed through pines toward a ridge. From the summit the whole coastline unrolled in blue and white. Our guide saved the final landmark for sunset, pointing ahead with pride, for beyond the gorge stood the most spectacular waterfall in the entire country.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Rain softened the soil overnight, so I carried the trowel and the twine out past the gate. Sparrows argued in the hedge while I turned the compost heap with a fork. The tomato vines needed tying, and I looped each stem gently with strips of cloth. Basil and chives crowded the near bed, shading the radish rows behind them. I thinned the carrot tops and piled the weeds into a canvas sack. A robin followed me along the path, darting after worms in the turned dirt. The hose had kinked near the barrel, so I straightened its coils and hung the nozzle up. Beans climbed their poles in spirals, gripping tight after the wind. I pinched suckers off the peppers and checked the underside of each leaf for aphids. Marigolds bordered the onion patch, bright against the dark mulch. The wheelbarrow rattled down the gravel walk loaded with prunings and stones. I swept the potting bench and stacked the clay pots by size. Seed packets were sorted into a tin box and labeled with a pencil. The pond pump hummed behind the reeds where tadpoles drifted. I scrubbed algae off the trough and refilled it to the brim. Cucumbers sprawled over the trellis, tangling with the morning glory vines. A bumblebee worked the squash blossoms slowly, row by row. I moved the shade cloth over the lettuce as the sun climbed high. The apple boughs hung low, heavy with unripe fruit. I propped one limb with a forked stick and tied it with twine. Potatoes hilled in long ridges ran straight toward the fence line. The shed door stuck, so I planed its edge and oiled the hinges. Tools were wiped, hung, and counted before lunch. After lunch I sowed parsley in a shallow drill and tamped the soil flat. The sprinkler ticked in arcs across the lawn, hissing softly. I edged the walk with shears and swept the clippings into the bin. Dusk brought moths to the porch lamp and cool air off the meadow. I locked the greenhouse, coiled the hose, and stacked the tools inside the shed.

The ledger showed a gap in travel claims that needed receipts. I phoned the depot about a delayed parcel and left a message. The blinds stuck halfway, letting a bar of sun across the carpet. Coffee ran out by eleven, and an intern fetched more from the corner shop. The printer queue stalled on a color chart, so I rebooted the spooler. A client arrived early and waited in the lobby with a briefcase. I drafted a memo about parking permits and pinned it up. The accountant reconciled the petty cash drawer coin by coin. I labeled folders for payroll, vendors, utilities, and insurance. The shredder growled through a stack of obsolete forms. A technician serviced the air unit and signed the work order. The directory was updated with two arrivals and one departure. I booked the van for Thursday and confirmed the driver by phone. The alarm panel beeped at noon and I punched in the code. Sandwiches arrived late, and the team ate standing around the table. The projector bulb dimmed during the slides, so we opened the shades. I proofread the newsletter and amended three captions. The safe was counted, locked, and entered in the log. Couriers came and went with padded envelopes all afternoon. I watered the lobby plants and dusted the reception desk. The clock buzzed for the fire drill, and we filed down the stairway. Attendance was tallied on a clipboard in the courtyard. Back inside, I answered queries about holiday rosters. The day closed with signatures, stamps, and I filed the receipts inside the cabinet.
